name: faccessat2
synopsis: int syscall(SYS_faccessat2, int dirfd, const char *pathname, int mode, int flags);
description: faccessat2 checks the calling process's permissions for a file relative to a directory file descriptor. It performs accessibility checks similar to faccessat but with direct kernel support for flags, ensuring proper handling in newer Linux kernels.

parameters.name: dirfd
parameters.description: Directory file descriptor for relative paths

parameters.name: pathname
parameters.description: Path to the file to check

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Specifies the accessibility checks (e.g., F_OK, R_OK, W_OK, X_OK)

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Flags for the operation, such as AT_EACCESS or AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW

return_value.success: Returns 0 if all requested permissions are granted or the file exists
return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set to indicate the error

errors.description: The requested access would be denied to the file or search permission is denied for a directory in the path
pathname is relative but dirfd is neither AT_FDCWD nor a valid file descriptor
pathname points outside the accessible address space
mode was incorrectly specified or invalid flag in flags
Too many symbolic links were encountered
A component of pathname does not exist or is a dangling symbolic link
A component used as a directory in pathname is not a directory
Write permission was requested to a file with the immutable flag set
Write permission was requested for a file on a read-only filesystem
Write access was requested to an executable which is being executed

bugs: The glibc wrapper for faccessat() in versions before 2.33 emulated functionality without considering ACLs, but faccessat2 avoids this by using the direct kernel system call; older Linux kernels had issues with X_OK tests for superusers.
